findings.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 uses invalid Ruby syntax `<%- end if %>` with no condition, causing existing-topic embeds to fail with a template syntax error; use `<%- end %>`.
app/models/post.rb:133 returns raw imported HTML without sanitization, allowing scripts and event-handler attributes to cause stored XSS when rendered.

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 calls `i.content.scrub` without supporting description or content:encoded fields or handling missing content, causing valid RSS items to abort polling and prevent subsequent imports.
app/models/topic_embed.rb:65–72 incorrectly rewrites protocol-relative URLs to the article host, breaking resources; resolve them against the article URL using URI.join.
app/models/topic_embed.rb:65–72 leaves path-relative URLs unresolved, causing them to resolve against the forum instead of the article URL; resolve them using URI.join.

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:133 returns raw imported HTML without sanitization, allowing scripts and event-handler attributes to cause stored XSS when rendered.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, when cook_method is raw_html, the cook method in app/models/post.rb returns `raw` directly without any sanitization. The raw content comes from RSS/Atom feeds or remote URLs via ruby-readability. In app/models/topic_embed.rb, the import method passes content with cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]. The ruby-readability library does filter tags (tags: %w[div p code pre h1 h2 h3 b em i strong a img]) but this doesn't prevent XSS via event handlers like onclick on allowed tags, or javascript: URLs in href attributes. The content is then rendered in views using `raw post.cooked` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb line 17). This is a legitimate stored XSS vulnerability - malicious content from external sources could include `` or `` which would execute when rendered.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:65–72 incorrectly rewrites protocol-relative URLs to the article host, breaking resources; resolve them against the article URL using URI.join.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 65-72, the method `absolutize_urls` handles URLs that start with '/'. The code checks `if src.present? && src.start_with?('/')` for img tags. Protocol-relative URLs start with '//' (e.g., '//example.com/image.jpg'). The regex `sub(/^/+/, '')` strips leading slashes, so '//example.com/image.jpg' becomes 'example.com/image.jpg' and then gets prefixed with the article host, resulting in something like 'http://eviltrout.com/example.com/image.jpg'. This is indeed incorrect behavior - protocol-relative URLs should be resolved differently (by just prepending the scheme). The finding correctly identifies a real bug where protocol-relative URLs would be incorrectly rewritten.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:65–72 leaves path-relative URLs unresolved, causing them to resolve against the forum instead of the article URL; resolve them using URI.join.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the absolutize_urls method in app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 53-72, the code checks if href/src start_with?('/') and then constructs the absolute URL as `#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^/+/, '')}`. This handles absolute-path URLs (starting with '/') correctly. However, the finding claims 'path-relative URLs' are unresolved - these would be URLs like 'images/wat.jpg' (no leading slash). The code only handles URLs starting with '/' and leaves truly relative URLs (without leading slash) unchanged. These would then resolve against the forum's base URL instead of the original article URL. This is a real bug - relative URLs without a leading slash won't be converted to absolute URLs.
